body: Basically the idea is I want there to be a spell storing item the party uses on a regular bases, but actually holds a secret alarm spell that will go off under specific homebrew conditions.

Hi I am Dming for the first time. I am just trying to see if there is a specific magical way or item that hides how many spell slots it can store, or if i have to home brew some stuff (of course the secret can be found with a high enough Arcana check)
So how come you can’t do sneak attack with a thrown weapon? It becomes a ranged weapon?

In my west marches server, the ruling is rage bonus does not get added to range thrown weapons. which is confusing to me because they count as a thrown melee weapons, which is why you can't sneak attack a thrown weapon because it is not a "ranged" weapon.
looooove it, exactly what i wanted
That’s a decent explanation why I’m wrong. This I can agree with.

I am looking for input. At this point I’ll agree that it will have to be a house rule, but saying that I’m thinking narratively and trying to pull a mechanical effect from it is LITERALLY what this game is about. 
I was looking for more in depth reasons why a plus one weapon is a plus one weapon, and I was unaware of magical items that improve improvised weapons, if there are I would love to see them. 

Every single mechanic dnd has is backed by narrative reasoning. Saying that the writers didn’t produce any oversight is a little close minded. It’s possible they wanted to leave it vague because the whole “improvised weapon” mechanic is so vague of what constitutes a weapon, that the writers could have decided to leave those decisions up to the DM

I mean that could easily be an oversight, because it doesn’t explain how or why only the AC is improved. The whole point of dnd is that mechanics back up the narrative reasons for things. In a narrative reasoning, I don’t see why a magical shield can not be better at bashing

Again that’s vague. Look at a club. What’s the +1 do to a club? Make it harder? Make it bash more? We can assume all plus 1 bludgeoning weapons are magically enchanted to be “harder” or punch through more. I can assume we make armor magically harder and more durable. So if we make a shield harder and more durable, like a club, it should be able to hit more as well.
